about: What the web app (web/app.js, as shell.ivrit) may ask of the native shells, and what they answer. Android (shell/android, Java) and iPhone (shell/ios, Swift) both implement all of it, under the plugin name below; scripts/check-native-api.mjs checks the three against this file. A method or event only one platform has says so in "platforms". Rejections carry the listed codes (err.code in the page). A method only some shells have names its "feature": a shell that has it lists the feature in notificationStatus().features, and the web app calls it only after checking that.

result.available: boolean: push can work at all (Firebase configured; on iPhone, always)
result.permission: "granted" | "denied" | "default" (never asked); "denied" also when turned off in the phone's settings
result.popup: boolean: messages show on screen (Android: the channel's importance; iPhone: banners allowed)
result.platform: "android" | "ios": for wording only (which settings to describe), never for behaviour
result.importance: number, Android only: the channel's importance
result.features: string[], optional: what this shell can do beyond the contract's common methods ("watchFolders")

result.transport: "fcm" | "apns": Communicator's name for the push service
result.token: the push service's token for this install (APNs: lowercase hex)
result.key: base64url of the 32-byte AES key messages are sealed with
result.previousToken: string, optional: the token this one replaced
result.environment: "production" | "sandbox", APNs only: which Apple service the token belongs to

options.communicator: Communicator's base URL, for acks and source logos
options.sources: [{id, name, name_he}]: names for notifications shown while the app is closed
options.site: this site's origin, where watched folders upload
options.appToken: the app's session token, which watched folders upload with

result.id: string, optional: the message a notification tap opened, once

options.interactive: boolean: may show Google's account picker

options.clientId: the server's (web) OAuth client, which the code is for

result.code: server auth code with offline access to drive.file, for POST /auth/drive

options.uploadId: the page's id for this upload; the same id again is the same upload
options.title: string

uploadShared.note: Superseded by enqueueTranscription; kept for older pages. Not called by the web app.

result.files: [{id, name, type, size, durationMs (-1 unknown), origin ("whatsapp" | ""), uploadId}]

result.watches: [{id, label (the phone's name for the folder), folder (My files folder id, "" the top), folderName, language, minSeconds, maxSeconds (0: none), wifiOnly, paused, since, lastChecked, quotaUntil, lastError ("" | "signin" | "quota" | "access" | "failed" | a server error key), sent, waiting}]

addWatch.note: Opens Android's folder picker; the app keeps access to the chosen folder only.

options.folder: My files folder id ("" the top)

result.watch: {id, label (the phone's name for the folder), folder (My files folder id, "" the top), folderName, language, minSeconds, maxSeconds (0: none), wifiOnly, paused, since, lastChecked, quotaUntil, lastError ("" | "signin" | "quota" | "access" | "failed" | a server error key), sent, waiting}

any of addWatch's options, and paused

result.watch: {id, label (the phone's name for the folder), folder (My files folder id, "" the top), folderName, language, minSeconds, maxSeconds (0: none), wifiOnly, paused, since, lastChecked, quotaUntil, lastError ("" | "signin" | "quota" | "access" | "failed" | a server error key), sent, waiting}

events.push: {}: a message arrived while the app was open
events.shared: {}: files were shared into the app
events.pushToken: {}: the push token changed; register again

watch.about: {id}: a watch's state changed (checked, sent, an error)
